# `deps/version-drift`

**A monorepo declares each dependency with one range**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Pack** | `@codelaw/rules-deps` (npm) · `codelaw-rules-deps` (PyPI) |
| **Languages** | JSON, TOML |
| **Turned on by** | `codelaw:deps/recommended` at `warn` |
| **Severity when named without one** | `error` |
| **Options** | none — severity only |
| **Fix** | `suggest` — `codelaw fix --unsafe` applies it; review the diff, it can change behaviour (aligning a range changes what that workspace installs; the lower range may be on purpose) |
| **Stability** | `preview` — runs only with `preview = true` |
| **Since** | 0.5.0 |
| **Files** | only `**/package.json`, `**/pyproject.toml` |

## What it checks

In a monorepo — npm, yarn or pnpm workspaces (`package.json` `workspaces`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml` `packages`), or a uv workspace (`[tool.uv.workspace] members`) — the same dependency declared with different ranges in different workspaces installs two versions, or one version some workspace was never tested with. The rule compares each dependency's range across the root manifest and every member: `dependencies`, `devDependencies` and `optionalDependencies` (never `peerDependencies`, which are wide on purpose), and `[project] dependencies`, `optional-dependencies` and `[dependency-groups]` (PyPI ranges by their clauses, so `>= 2.31` and `>=2.31.0` agree). A range with a protocol (`workspace:`, `file:`, a URL) is not compared.

Each manifest whose range is not the target gets a finding, and the fix rewrites it to the target:

```toml
[deps.drift]
policy = "highest"          # the range whose floor is highest (default); "root": the root manifest's
ignore = ["npm:typescript"] # never compared
```

**Why:** One version per dependency is one set of bugs, one set of types and one upgrade.

## Configuration

Everything below goes in `codelaw.toml` at the repo root. The same keys work as `[tool.codelaw]` in `pyproject.toml` or `"codelaw"` in `package.json` ([SR-CONFIG](../../../records/0110_config.md)).

### Turn it on

**Install the pack** (`codelaw init` does it for the languages it finds):

```bash
npm install --save-dev @codelaw/rules-deps
pip install codelaw-rules-deps
```

**Then extend a preset that turns it on** — `codelaw:deps/recommended` sets it to `warn`:

```toml
preview = true                        # pack rules are preview today
extends = ["codelaw:deps/recommended"]
```

- **A rule exists only once its pack is loaded** through `extends`; naming it in `[rules]` without that is an unknown rule id (exit 2).
- **Without `preview = true`** the rule is skipped and codelaw warns that it is preview.

### Severity

```toml
[rules]
"deps/version-drift" = "warn"    # error | warn | info | off
```

- **`error`** fails the run (exit 1) · **`warn`** fails only with `--max-warnings N` · **`info`** never fails · **`off`** turns it off.
- **Naming it with a severity turns it on** even when no preset does.

### For a group of files

A `[scope.<name>]` gives some files their own setting, applied after `[rules]` — a scope of your own needs `files`:

```toml
[scope.legacy]
files = ["src/legacy/**/*.json"]
rules = { "deps/version-drift" = "off" }
```

A scope's `remap` changes whole severities in its files, after everything else: `remap = { error = "warn" }` never fails the run there.

### Warn locally, fail in CI

The `ci` profile runs when `CI` is set; `local` otherwise; `--profile <name>` or `CODELAW_PROFILE` picks one.

```toml
[profile.local.rules]
"deps/version-drift" = "warn"

[profile.ci.rules]
"deps/version-drift" = "error"
```

### In `pyproject.toml` or `package.json`

```toml
# pyproject.toml
[tool.codelaw.rules]
"deps/version-drift" = { severity = "warn" }
```

```json
{
  "codelaw": {
    "rules": {
      "deps/version-drift": {"severity": "warn"}
    }
  }
}
```

### Silence one finding

An inline `codelaw-ignore` always needs a reason; `expires=`, `warn_days=` and `by=` date it ([SR-LINTER](../../../records/0106_linter.md) decision 6).

- **JSON** has no comments: switch the rule off for the file with a scope, or use the baseline.
- **TOML:** `# codelaw-ignore deps/version-drift: <reason>`
- **Dated:** `# codelaw-ignore deps/version-drift expires=2026-12-31 by=you@example.com: <reason>`

### Keep today's findings, fail on new ones

```bash
codelaw baseline add --rule deps/version-drift --expires 2026-12-31 --reason "<why>"
```

See [SR-BASELINE](../../../records/0104_baseline-and-deprecations.md).

### See what applies

```bash
codelaw explain deps/version-drift       # what it wants, why, how to fix
codelaw check --rule deps/version-drift  # only this rule
codelaw config --print --for <file>      # the resolved setting, and where it came from
```

## How to fix

1. Run `codelaw fix --unsafe` to align the range, or edit it by hand.
2. Run the install so the lockfile follows.
3. If a workspace needs another version on purpose, add the package to `[deps.drift] ignore`.

## Examples

### JSON

#### Don't

```json
// package.json
{
  "private": true,
  "workspaces": ["packages/*"]
}
// packages/web/package.json
{
  "dependencies": {
    "react": "^18.2.0"
  }
}
// packages/app/package.json
{
  "dependencies": {
    "react": "^18.3.1"
  }
}
```

#### Do

```json
// package.json
{
  "private": true,
  "workspaces": ["packages/*"]
}
// packages/web/package.json
{
  "dependencies": {
    "react": "^18.3.1"
  }
}
// packages/app/package.json
{
  "dependencies": {
    "react": "^18.3.1"
  }
}
```

### TOML

#### Don't

```toml
# pyproject.toml
[project]
name = "mono"
dependencies = ["httpx>=0.27"]

[tool.uv.workspace]
members = ["libs/*"]
# libs/core/pyproject.toml
[project]
name = "core"
dependencies = ["httpx>=0.25"]
```

#### Do

```toml
# pyproject.toml
[project]
name = "mono"
dependencies = ["httpx>=0.27"]

[tool.uv.workspace]
members = ["libs/*"]
# libs/core/pyproject.toml
[project]
name = "core"
dependencies = ["httpx>=0.27"]
```
